items.title: NADPH oxidase 4 as a source of hydrogen peroxide can regulate norepinephrine levels and vascular contraction.
items.abstract: The adrenal glands play a pivotal role in maintaining physiological homeostasis, and disturbance in their function can lead to significant clinical disorders, including hypertension, and adrenal insufficiency. Reactive oxygen species (ROS), once considered merely byproducts of cellular metabolism, are now recognized as critical signaling molecules within the adrenal cortex and medulla. Among the major enzymatic sources of ROS are NADPH oxidases (Nox). Dysregulation of Nox-derived ROS has been linked to altered steroidogenesis, oxidative stress- mediated adrenal damage, and tumorigenic processes. We aimed to elucidate the role of Nox4 on adrenal function under healthy conditions. Using Nox4-knockout mouse model, adrenal effects were assessed by histological analysis, real-time PCR, and cathecholamine quantification using HPLC-ECD and LC-MS/MS. Cardiovascular function was evaluated by echocardiography, blood pressure measurements, and ex vivo vascular function analysis. Here, we demonstrated that Nox4 is expressed in the mouse adrenal gland, and its deletion led to decreased hydrogen peroxide production, diminished dopamine beta-hydroxylase mRNA expression, and reduced norepinephrine levels. In chromaffin cells, treatment with hydrogen peroxide stimulated catecholamine release and increased dopamine beta-hydroxylase expression, indicating a regulatory role of hydrogen peroxide in catecholamine synthesis and secretion. Further analysis of the physiological consequences of reduced norepinephrine levels in Nox4 -/- mice revealed decreased alpha-1 adrenergic receptor expression and impaired adrenergic vascular contraction, while cardiac function remained unaffected. In a model of physical activity, Nox4 depletion resulted in smaller adrenal glands and lower urinary norepinephrine concentrations, further explaining diminished physical activity of Nox4 -/- mice. Our findings provide evidence that Nox4-derived H 2 O 2 plays a role in norepinephrine release and norepinephrine-mediated functions. Hence, loss of Nox4 impairs vascular contractility and reduces physical activity performance, highlighting the physiological importance of Nox4 in adrenal function.

items.title: The Most Recent European and American Guidelines on Cardiac Rehabilitation: A Lack of Focus on Diaphragm Training.
items.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) are the leading causes of death and morbidity worldwide. Patients with vascular and cardiac conditions undergo cardiac rehabilitation (CR), a process that may begin before surgery (less frequently), after invasive procedures, or as part of chronic disease management, with durations varying by healthcare facilities or national policies. CR is a valuable non-pharmacological intervention that supports patient health and the resumption of daily activities. These rehabilitation programmes are strongly recommended for cardiac patients and are structured according to guidelines from organisations such as the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and the American Heart Association/American Association of Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Rehabilitation (AHA/AACPR). This editorial reviews the latest ESC and AHA/AACPR guidelines, emphasising physical activities such as endurance and resistance training, while highlighting the lack of detail on inspiratory muscle training (IMT). The editorial reiterates the Italian Association of Cardiovascular Rehabilitation (AIRC) proposals regarding IMT and calls for further clinical trials.

items.title: GLP-1 RA Eligibility in Reproductive-Age U.S. Women.
items.abstract: Use of glucagon-like peptide 1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) for diabetes or weight management may affect pregnancy outcomes. We sought to estimate the number of U.S. women of reproductive age eligible for GLP-1 RA therapy. Using 2017-2023 nationally representative survey data, we identified nonpregnant U.S. women aged 18-44 years who met trial-based eligibility criteria for diabetes, weight management, or secondary cardiovascular prevention. Among 3,218 participants, 1,447 were eligible for GLP-1 RAs, representing 24.6 million U.S. women. Among GLP-1 RA-eligible women, mean BMI was 34.8 kg/m 2 , 8.3% had diabetes, and 1.9% had prior cardiovascular disease. Eligibility was primarily for weight management (24.1 million), followed by diabetes (2.0 million) and cardiovascular prevention (0.34 million). Nearly half of U.S. reproductive-age women are eligible for GLP-1 RAs. Given limited pregnancy safety data and rising cardiometabolic burden in reproductive-age women, research is needed to guide counseling and coverage of preconception GLP-1 RA use. items.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Once-Weekly Insulin Efsitora Alfa in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
items.abstract: Achieving and maintaining a glycated hemoglobin (HbA 1c ) level <7% in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D) remains challenging, partly because of the daily insulin injection burden. Insulin efsitora alfa is a long-acting insulin Fc-fusion protein designed for once-weekly administration, which may reduce injection burden. The purpose of this analysis is to evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly insulin efsitora alfa compared with once-daily basal insulin in adults with T2D, stratified by baseline insulin use. PubMed, Web of Science, Scopus, and Cochrane CENTRAL were searched from inception through July 2025, along with ClinicalTrials.gov. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) enrolling adults with T2D that compared once-weekly insulin efsitora alfa with once-daily basal insulin for ≥12 weeks were included. Six trials met eligibility criteria. Two authors independently extracted data using a standardized form. The primary outcome was the mean change in HbA 1c (%). Secondary outcomes included fasting plasma glucose, body weight, time in range, hypoglycemia, and adverse events. Risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. Six RCTs, including 4,116 participants, were analyzed. Efsitora demonstrated HbA 1c reduction comparable to daily basal insulin in insulin-treated patients (mean difference [MD] -0.06% [95% CI -0.24, 0.11]; P = 0.48) and insulin-naive patients (MD -0.03% [95% CI -0.12, 0.06]; P = 0.51). Nocturnal hypoglycemia episodes were fewer with efsitora in both insulin-treated patients (risk ratio [RR] 0.82 [95% CI 0.68, 0.98]; P = 0.03) and insulin-naive patients (RR 0.71 [95% CI 0.52, 0.95]; P = 0.02). All included trials were open-label, and follow-up duration was limited. Long-term outcomes, real-world adherence, and cost-effectiveness could not be fully assessed. Once-weekly insulin efsitora alfa demonstrates glycemic control and overall safety comparable to once-daily basal insulin in adults with T2D, with fewer nocturnal hypoglycemia episodes. Longer-term RCTs and real-world studies are needed to define its long-term clinical and economic impact.

items.title: Totally Thoracoscopic Atrial Fibrillation Ablation With the Gemini S Bipolar Clamp: A Single-Center Descriptive Cohort Study of 1-Year Rhythm, Safety, and Quality-of-Life Outcomes.
items.abstract: Outcome data for the Gemini S bipolar radiofrequency clamp are almost absent; the only indexed report being a three-patient case series. We describe 1-year outcomes in a consecutive cohort. We retrospectively analyzed all consecutive patients treated with the Gemini S clamp between January 2021 and August 2024. Epicardial box isolation was combined with left atrial appendage (LAA) exclusion; completeness was confirmed by entry and exit block on epicardial three-dimensional mapping. The primary outcome was freedom from AF recurrence at 12 months, on and off antiarrhythmic drugs (AADs) after a 90-day blanking period. Twenty-three patients were included (mean age 64.4 ± 8.0 years; 82.6% male). AF was paroxysmal in 34.8%, persistent in 26.1%, and long-standing persistent in 39.1%; 60.9% had prior catheter ablation and 69.6% had failed or were intolerant to a Class I or III agent. A complete block-verified box lesion was achieved in 95.7% and LAA exclusion in 91.3%. Three patients (13.0%) required conversion to sternotomy for bleeding, exceeding larger series. There was no death, stroke, phrenic nerve palsy, or pacemaker implantation. At 1 year, 87.0% (95% CI 67.9-95.5) were in sinus rhythm, all off Class I/III AADs. Sinus rhythm was achieved in 87.0% of patients at 1 year. As the largest reported experience with this device, the series provides device-level evidence where little existed, but it is descriptive, not powered for comparison, and the conversion rate needs confirmation.

items.title: Global research landscape of ferroptosis in colorectal cancer: a multi-database bibliometric analysis (2017-2025).
items.abstract: Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death, has attracted increasing attention in recent years because of its critical roles in tumor progression, therapeutic resistance, and immune regulation. Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the most prevalent malignancies worldwide and imposes a substantial mortality burden. This study aimed to systematically analyze the global research landscape, hotspots, and developmental trends of ferroptosis in CRC research from 2017 to 2025. English-language publications related to ferroptosis and CRC published between January 1, 2017, and December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) and Scopus databases. A total of 1, 354 original articles and reviews were included. VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix package in R were used for bibliometric and visualization analyses to evaluate annual publication trends, country/region and institutional collaboration networks, author contributions, journal distribution, co-cited references, keyword co-occurrence, and thematic evolution. The number of publications in this field increased rapidly after 2020 and peaked in 2025. China ranked first in both publication output and total citations, followed by the United States, and China-United States collaboration constituted the core of the international collaboration network. Central South University was the most productive institution, while journals such as Frontiers in Oncology and Frontiers in Immunology served as major publication platforms. Research hotspots were mainly concentrated on chemotherapy resistance, the tumor immune microenvironment, PANoptosis, prognostic models, non-coding RNAs, gut microbiota, and the regulation of ferroptosis by traditional Chinese medicine and natural products. Ferroptosis has become a rapidly evolving frontier in CRC research. The research focus is gradually shifting from fundamental molecular mechanisms toward translational medical directions, including chemosensitization, combination immunotherapy, reversal of drug resistance, and precise prognostic evaluation. This study provides a systematic reference for understanding the global knowledge structure and future research directions in the field of ferroptosis and CRC.

items.title: Emerging innovative immunotherapies in malignant ascites: current landscape, challenges and perspectives.
items.abstract: Malignant ascites is a common, severe complication of advanced solid tumors, driven by multifactorial pathogenesis, including impaired lymphatic drainage, vascular endothelial growth factor-induced vascular hyperpermeability, pro-permeability inflammatory cytokines, and profound peritoneal immunosuppression. Clinically, it correlates with poor prognosis, reduced overall survival, and substantial quality-of-life deterioration. Current treatment remains predominantly palliative: repeated large-volume paracentesis offers transient symptom relief, fails to prevent reaccumulation, and carries procedural risks. Emerging evidence indicates malignant ascites is not merely passive fluid accumulation but an active, immunosuppressive niche shaped by bidirectional crosstalk among tumor cells, stromal components, diverse immune subsets (e.g., regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, dysfunctional CD8 + T cells), and soluble mediators. This narrative review summarizes recent advances in immunomodulatory treatment for malignant ascites, with an emphasis on strategies targeting the ascitic immune microenvironment. Intraperitoneal administration of immune checkpoint inhibitors has shown acceptable safety and preliminary activity in early-phase single-arm trials, although confirmatory data from larger controlled studies are lacking. In randomized trials, the T-cell engager catumaxomab prolonged puncture-free survival, while the bispecific antibody M701 has shown similar benefits in a phase II randomized controlled study; these findings support further investigation of localized T-cell redirection. Preclinical and early-phase clinical studies suggest that intraperitoneal oncolytic viruses can induce immunogenic tumor cell death and T-cell activation, with single-cell analyses indicating remodeling of the ascitic immune microenvironment. Future directions include integrating ascites immune phenotyping, patient-derived organoids for drug sensitivity testing, and machine learning-based decision support to guide personalized immunotherapy.

items.title: Ivonescimab combined with radiotherapy in the treatment of advanced lung adenocarcinoma with high expression of PD-L1: A case report.
items.abstract: The optimal sequencing of immunotherapy and radiotherapy in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains unclear. The present study reports a case of advanced lung adenocarcinoma (cT4N2bM1a, stage IVa) with a programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) tumor proportion score of 90% and TP53 mutation. The patient received first-line ivonescimab monotherapy (900 mg, every 3 weeks) for four cycles, achieving a partial response (47% reduction per Response Evaluation Criteria in Solid Tumors 1.1). Sequential thoracic radiotherapy (5,000 cGy/25 fractions) was then administered for consolidation. Serum tumor markers (carcinoembryonic antigen, cancer antigen 125, cytokeratin 19 fragment and neuron-specific enolase) exhibited markedly decreased levels from baseline. Grade I radiation pneumonitis occurred post-radiotherapy but resolved rapidly with low-dose glucocorticoids. At the last follow-up (8 months), the patient remained progression-free with the Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status improving from 2 to 0. This case provides real-world evidence for the 'immunotherapy induction followed by radiotherapy consolidation' strategy in an individual with high PD-L1 expression. The presence of TP53 mutation may predict an enhanced synergistic response to combined immunotherapy and radiotherapy, warranting further investigation.

items.title: In vivo CAR-T for the treatment of autoimmune diseases: Current progress and future directions.
items.abstract: Autoimmune diseases are a clinical challenge because current immunosuppressive therapies fail to eliminate pathogenic immunocytes, such as autoreactive B cells, plasma cells, and antigen-presenting cells, which induce chronic inflammation. Chimeric antigen receptor T (CAR-T) cell therapy offers a targeted strategy to eliminate these disease-driving populations. Early ex vivo CAR-T cell studies on severe autoimmunity have shown effective B-cell depletion and sustained remission. However, its toxicity, cost, and lengthy manufacturing process limit its widespread clinical use. In vivo CAR-T technologies-using viral vectors or mRNA lipid nanoparticles to generate CAR-T cells directly within the patient-aim to overcome these barriers. Preclinical and emerging clinical data indicate that these platforms can rapidly reprogram circulating T cells, induce potent B-cell clearance, and achieve clinical improvement in refractory diseases. Viral vectors provide durable expression but raise integration and immunogenicity concerns, whereas mRNA-LNP systems enable transient, controllable CAR expression with greater manufacturing scalability. These advances have positioned in vivo CAR-T cells as a promising therapeutic strategy for autoimmune diseases. Continuing progress in delivery specificity, safety engineering, trial design, and cost-effective production is essential for translating this approach into widely accessible treatments. In this review, we synthesized preclinical and emerging clinical evidence, compared delivery platforms, and proposed practical recommendations for safety engineering, trial design, and manufacturing, which will help guide future translational efforts and accelerate clinical adoption.

items.title: Resveratrol as an immune checkpoint inhibitor to enhance the efficacy of breast cancer immunotherapy.
items.abstract: A major goal in cancer treatment is to convert "cold" tumors into "hot" ones by altering the tumor microenvironment (TME). Breast cancer is often a cold tumor and is resistant to immunotherapy. Resveratrol is a polyphenolic compound found in grapes, with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and potential cardioprotective and anti-aging properties. Resveratrol promotes the conversion of immunologically cold breast tumors into hot tumors, thereby increasing the efficacy of immunotherapy. This article reviews the potential of resveratrol to convert immunologically "cold" breast tumors into "hot" tumors by modulating the TME and enhancing the efficacy of immunotherapy. A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar to identify English-language articles investigating the effects of resveratrol on immune checkpoints in breast cancer. The results showed that resveratrol suppresses key cancer-promoting pathways (PI3K/Akt/mTOR, MAPK/ERK, STAT/NF-κB, and Wnt/β-catenin) and modulates the immune system. It boosts anti-tumor immunity by activating immunostimulatory cells (such as M1-TAMs, NKs, and CTLs) while simultaneously inhibiting immunosuppressive cells (such as Tregs and MDSCs). It also acts as a natural immune checkpoint inhibitor by targeting the PD-1/PD-L1 pathway. Resveratrol prevents T-cell exhaustion in "cold" tumors and reduces PD-L1 expression in "hot" tumors, thereby enhancing cytotoxic T cells' ability to attack cancer. However, its effectiveness is limited by poor bioavailability and differences in the biological activity of its metabolites. Future clinical studies are needed to confirm these results and determine optimal therapeutic protocols for resveratrol-mediated breast cancer immunotherapy.

items.title: Community health workers and promotores de salud : a tiered framework for infectious disease prevention and care among California agricultural workers.
items.abstract: Agricultural workers in the United States face a disproportionate burden of infectious diseases, including tuberculosis, HIV, coccidioidomycosis, viral hepatitis, and COVID-19, driven by occupational exposures, crowded housing, poverty, and limited healthcare access. Despite this burden, farmworkers have among the lowest rates of healthcare utilization of any US working population, and traditional clinic-based delivery models are poorly suited to the realities of agricultural labor. Community health workers (CHWs), known as promotores de salud in Latino communities, offer a well-established strategy for bridging this gap through shared language, culture, and lived experience with the communities they serve. This mini-review synthesizes evidence on CHW and promotora interventions for infectious disease prevention and care among agricultural workers, with particular attention to California's farmworker communities. Available evidence supports CHW roles in COVID-19 vaccination and outreach, tuberculosis treatment adherence through community-based directly observed therapy, HIV prevention and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) navigation, and hepatitis screening and linkage to care. However, existing programs have largely operated in isolation, and, to our knowledge, no CHW intervention for coccidioidomycosis has been developed despite its importance as an occupational infectious disease in California. To address this fragmentation, we propose a three-tiered framework that extends CHW roles from community-based prevention and early recognition to screening, linkage, and treatment support, and ultimately to formal integration with healthcare and public health systems. Implementing this framework will require infectious disease-specific training in the languages of the communities served, sustainable financing, and rigorous evaluation of an integrated cross-disease CHW model in California's agricultural communities.

items.title: Etiology-associated differences in the gut microbiome and metabolome in hepatocellular carcinoma: an exploratory study of alcohol-related and HBV-related cases.
items.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) arises in heterogeneous etiological contexts, but direct cross-omics comparisons between HCC subgroups defined by different etiologies remain limited. In this exploratory study, we combined fecal 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted serum metabolomics with exploratory cross-omics analyses to compare gut microbial composition, serum metabolic profiles, and microbiome-metabolite association patterns between hepatitis B virus-related HCC (HBV-HCC) and alcohol-related HCC (ALD-HCC). Forty patients who underwent primary tumor resection were included, comprising 26 with HBV-HCC and 14 with ALD-HCC. Alpha diversity indices did not differ significantly between groups, whereas within-group Bray-Curtis dissimilarity was greater in ALD-HCC and genus-level beta-diversity ordination showed only modest separation between the two groups. LEfSe-based screening suggested the enrichment of candidate taxa, including Faecalibacterium , Roseburia , Lachnospira , Turicibacter , and Butyribacter in HBV-HCC, whereas Allisonella and Coprobacillus were enriched in ALD-HCC. Untargeted metabolomics showed group separation in supervised models and identified exploratory candidate metabolic features mainly involving glycerophospholipid metabolism, primary bile acid biosynthesis, aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis, and central carbon metabolism in cancer; however, these metabolite-level findings did not remain significant after multiple-testing correction. Procrustes and O2PLS analyses indicated limited global concordance between the microbiome and metabolome, although exploratory associations were observed between several phosphatidylcholine-related features and microbial taxa. Overall, HBV-HCC and ALD-HCC may be associated with different gut microbial and serum metabolic patterns, and these findings should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating.

items.title: Congenital Bile Acid Synthesis Defect Type 2 Mimicking Biliary Atresia: A Case Report of Delta-4-3-Oxosteroid 5-Beta-Reductase Deficiency in a Two-Month-Old Infant.
items.abstract: Neonatal cholestasis presents a complex diagnostic challenge, frequently necessitating the differentiation of numerous etiologies, including the anatomically correctable biliary atresia (BA), from various metabolic and genetic disorders. The timely and accurate identification of inborn errors of bile acid metabolism is particularly critical, as these conditions can lead to progressive liver damage if left untreated. Congenital bile acid synthesis defects (CBASDs) are rare autosomal recessive inborn errors of metabolism that can manifest as neonatal cholestasis. Their clinical and biochemical profile, particularly in cases of normal or low gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) in the setting of significant cholestasis, can mimic other causes of neonatal liver disease, most notably BA, thereby posing a significant diagnostic challenge. We report a two-month-old male infant presenting with early-onset cholestatic jaundice since day 20 of life. Clinical and ultrasonographic findings initially raised strong suspicion for BA. However, the biochemical profile of markedly elevated transaminases, cholestasis with normal-to-low GGT, massive hyperferritinemia, and relatively low total bile acids suggested a metabolic etiology. Urine bile acid profiling by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry revealed trace levels of primary bile acids with accumulation of Δ4-3-oxo intermediates. Next-generation sequencing has confirmed the diagnosis of CBASD type 2. Liver biopsy demonstrated giant cell hepatitis without ductal proliferation, thus definitively excluding BA and precluding the need for a Kasai portoenterostomy.

items.title: Virus-encoded circular RNAs in human cancer: mechanisms and clinical implications.
items.abstract: Circular RNAs (circRNAs) are covalently closed RNA molecules generated mainly through back-splicing. Their resistance to exonuclease-mediated degradation, cell-type specificity, and regulatory versatility make them important participants in both host and viral biology. Since the initial demonstration that circular DNA tumor viruses produce abundant circRNAs, an expanding repertoire of virus-encoded circular RNAs (viro-circRNAs) has been identified in Epstein-Barr virus (EBV), Kaposi sarcoma-associated herpesvirus (KSHV), human papillomavirus (HPV), hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), and related animal tumor viruses. Accumulating evidence indicates that viro-circRNAs are not passive transcriptional by-products; rather, they function as miRNA sponges, RNA-binding protein scaffolds, modulators of RNA stability and transcription, epigenetic or epitranscriptomic regulators, and in selected cases, templates for viral peptide or oncoprotein translation. Recent studies have refined this field by revealing noncanonical herpesvirus-driven circRNA biogenesis, EBV circRPMS1-mediated METTL3 activation and p53 interaction, hypoxia-induced EBV circLMP2A-driven angiogenesis, HPV16 circE7-mediated immune evasion through promoter histone modification, HBV-derived circRNA signaling in hepatocellular carcinoma, and HCV-derived circRNAs that support viral RNA amplification. In this review, we synthesize current evidence using a mechanistic and clinically oriented framework: first defining viro-circRNA biogenesis and validation, then summarizing virus- and cancer-specific expression patterns, followed by a detailed analysis of direct tumor-cell mechanisms, tumor microenvironment remodeling, biomarker potential, therapeutic opportunities, and unresolved challenges. This framework is intended to move the discussion beyond descriptive cataloguing and toward testable hypotheses for translational viro-circRNA research.
items.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology

items.title: Suspected fibrosing cholestatic hepatitis in an immunocompetent child with hepatitis C: Case report.
items.abstract: A 12-year-old boy presented to our center with elevated aminotransferases, jaundice, right upper quadrant tenderness, and hepatomegaly. Evaluation revealed a highly elevated blood hepatitis C virus (HCV) ribonucleic acid (RNA) level, and liver biopsy showed canalicular and intrahepatic cholestasis, feathery degeneration of hepatocytes, and periportal/perisinusoidal fibrosis. Though there were atypical biopsy features, including absence of bile ductular reaction, we diagnosed suspected fibrosing cholestatic hepatitis (FCH). FCH secondary to HCV infection has been reported exclusively in immunosuppressed adults. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case of suspected FCH in a child, and the first reported case of suspected HCV-related FCH in any immunocompetent patient. Our patient was successfully treated with sofosbuvir/velpatasvir with sustained virologic response at 12 weeks. We conclude that FCH should be considered on the differential whenever any child with HCV infection presents with evidence of worsening liver injury including new hepatomegaly or jaundice.

items.title: Nidogen 1-enriched extracellular vesicles drive HCC progression by inducing mregDC differentiation and Treg infiltration.
items.abstract: Aim: Nidogen 1 (NID1) is a secreted pro-tumorigenic protein. While extracellular vesicle (EV)-NID1 is known to accelerate hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) progression, its role in reshaping the HCC immune microenvironment remains undefined. This study investigated how EV-NID1 modulates dendritic cells (DCs) to establish an immunosuppressive niche that drives liver cancer growth. Methods: The TIMER3.0 database was used to assess the correlations of NID1 with DCs and regulatory T cells (Tregs). A Transwell co-culture system using bone marrow-derived DCs was employed to evaluate the paracrine effects of HCC cells. EVs were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation, and their identity and purity were verified. Orthotopic and subcutaneous HCC mouse models were established to assess immune cell infiltration in vivo . DC adoptive transfer and Treg depletion assays were conducted to elucidate the underlying mechanism. Results: High NID1 expression in HCC was associated with increased infiltration of myeloid DCs and Tregs, and their co-occurrence predicted poor patient survival. In vitro , EV-NID1 induced DC maturation and promoted their polarization toward mature DCs enriched in immunoregulatory molecules (mregDC), accompanied by elevated secretion of C-C chemokine ligand 17 (CCL17). These polarized DCs promoted CD4 + T cell proliferation and FOXP3 + Treg formation. In vivo , NID1-high tumors exhibited accelerated growth and increased infiltration of mregDCs and Tregs in tumors, lymph nodes, and spleens. NID1 knockdown reduced tumor growth, whereas adoptive transfer of EV-NID1-pulsed DCs partially rescued tumor progression. Furthermore, Treg depletion markedly suppressed the growth of NID1-high tumors. Conclusions: This study suggests that NID1-enriched EVs derived from HCC promote tumor progression by inducing a regulatory phenotype in DCs and the expansion of Tregs.
items.journal: Extracellular vesicles and circulating nucleic acids

items.title: A Rare Finding of Pulmonary Epithelioid Hemangioendothelioma.
items.abstract: Epithelioid hemangioendothelioma (EHE) is a rare vascular tumor with variable presentation and malignancy. These highly uncommon tumors may arise from the liver, soft tissues, bones, and, more infrequently, from the lungs. Given its rarity, treatment approach is not unanimous, with ongoing debate regarding the relative benefits of surgical resection and radiation therapy. In support of growing efforts to standardize treatment of these tumors, we present our findings of a rare pulmonary EHE, incidentally detected in the left lung of a 65-year-old, nonsmoking female patient with a history of diabetes, hypertension, and renal cell carcinoma (RCC) in remission for 8 years after surgical resection. A surgical route was recommended, and left robot-assisted thoracoscopic wedge resections were performed. Final pathological assessment confirmed two pulmonary EHE tumors, one resected from the left upper lobe (LUL) and another from the left lower lobe (LLL) of the lung. Her postoperative course was uneventful, and at 13 months postresection, there has been no evidence of recurrence.

items.title: Penile metastasis from urothelial carcinoma of the bladder: An exceptionally rare localization.
items.abstract: Penile metastasis from urothelial carcinoma is exceedingly rare (<1%) and typically indicates advanced disseminated disease. We report a 60-year-old male who underwent radical cystoprostatectomy for high-grade urothelial carcinoma (pT4aN1). Before adjuvant chemotherapy, he developed indurated violaceous penile nodules, biopsy-confirmed as cutaneous metastasis. Staging CT revealed systemic relapse involving lungs, liver, and bone. As he was ineligible for cisplatin, he received gemcitabine-carboplatin, since enfortumab vedotin was unavailable locally. This case highlights the aggressive potential of high-grade urothelial carcinoma and the importance of prompt histological evaluation of unusual penile lesions in bladder cancer patients.

items.title: Palmitoyltransferase DHHC13 controls lysosomal cholesterol egress through palmitoylating Niemann-Pick C1.
items.abstract: Protein S-palmitoylation provides a key regulatory mechanism for diverse cellular activities. Although palmitoylated proteins are frequently observed in cholesterol-enriched membrane microdomains, how protein palmitoylation reciprocally regulates cholesterol metabolism remains elusive. Here, we identify DHHC13 as a critical regulator linking protein palmitoylation to lysosomal cholesterol egress. Through an shRNA screen, we found that lack of DHHC13 led to pronounced lysosomal cholesterol accumulation. Mechanistically, DHHC13 directly palmitoylated Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Loss of palmitoylation disrupted NPC1 association with lysosomes and caused its degradation, thereby impairing lysosomal cholesterol egress. Dhhc13 -/- mice phenocopied Npc1 -/- mice, displaying cholesterol deposition in the brain, liver, spleen, and kidney, along with significant Purkinje cell loss. Furthermore, two clinically relevant DHHC13 mutants (Q173H and R451Q) associated with neurodegenerative disorders showed diminished catalytic activity and failed to restore NPC1 palmitoylation or lysosomal cholesterol egress. Collectively, our findings uncover DHHC13 as a critical regulator of lysosomal cholesterol metabolism via NPC1 palmitoylation, providing mechanistic insights into cholesterol-related neurological disorders.
